title: Replaced: Don't replace your team with AI, multiply it and hire for psychology
summary: Ruben argues AI raises demand for knowledge work (Jevons Paradox), so the goal is making 5 people do the work of 50, not cutting headcount. He shows how he duplicated himself with AI tools, trained a team via recorded demos and SOPs, and hires for openness, humility and taste over technical credentials. The list of jobs AI will kill is paywalled.

principles.text: Ask how your team can do the work of 50 with AI, not how to replace people with AI.
principles.quote: Start thinking: “**How can 5 members of my team do the work of 50 with AI?**”

principles.text: Cheaper cognition expands demand for work (Jevons Paradox), so efficiency creates more projects and growth.
principles.quote: Cheaper/more efficient cognition → companies do way more projects, experiments, personalization, long-tail ideas that were once too expensive.

principles.text: Even at 10x efficiency you are capped by hours, so hire people to use AI for you.
principles.quote: Even if AI makes me 10x more efficient, I can’t have 10x more hours.

principles.text: Don't wait for perfect AI. Pick one real task (like research) and make it 10x better today.
Teach AI workflows top-down: record yourself doing it, then write an SOP the team can follow.
principles.quote: I create a Loom/Screen Studio video of me actually doing it.

principles.text: Hire for psychology (humility, resilience, taste, openness), not AI certifications.
principles.quote: Wrong: Look for “AI experts” with degrees/certifications.
